_comment: The flash-time offset checks. flashtool's -s/--status probe (connect_btl(), skip send/verify/finish) lets flash_katapult refuse a mismatched write before -f is ever called - see _verify_offset_before_write. _report_offset_mismatch is the second line of defence, checking again from what -f itself reported, for the board changing between the probe and the write; by the time that one runs the write has already happened, so it can only report, never refuse.

mutations.name: the pre-write probe is wired into the write path

mutations._comment: -s is the whole reason this call is safe to act on - it is what makes connect_btl() skip send_file/verify_file/finish. Losing it turns the 'probe' into an unflagged real write.
mutations.name: the probe passes -s, so it never actually writes
a mismatch found before writing is refused, not waved through

mutations._comment: The build-time half. Without a recorded app_address there is nothing to compare a probe or a handshake against, so this guard is what makes either check possible at all rather than something that would always read as 'nothing to compare'.
mutations.name: the build's own application address is read from the built .config

mutations._comment: force overriding a genuine mismatch is a deliberate, single-device decision. Letting it leak into a whole-type or update-all batch would let one board's exception silently force every board in the batch past a check that exists specifically to stop a fleet-wide brick.
mutations.name: a whole-type or update-all batch never carries force, only a single device does
